slides.0.title: Regulations and labels
slides.0.subtitle: DO tiers and Costa / Entre Cordilleras / Andes
slides.1.title: The DO framework
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Decreto 464
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Published on 26 May 1995 and administered by the SAG (agriculture and livestock service), it set up Chile's Denomination of Origin (DO) framework (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The main DO valleys
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Copiapó, Huasco, Elqui, Limarí, Choapa, Aconcagua, Casablanca, San Antonio (incl. Leyda), Maipo, Cachapoal, Colchagua, Curicó, Maule, Itata, Bío-Bío and Malleco
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Tier names to be checked
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The formal tiers (Región → Subregión → Zona → Área) are not tested yet; check them against the SAG text
slides.1.content: Chile's DOs are based on valleys and administered under decree by the SAG.
slides.2.title: Percentages on the label
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The 75% rule
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A stated place, variety or vintage must each be at least 75% accurate; up to 25% may come from elsewhere (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The 2011 amendment
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth says a 2011 amendment "refined" the labelling rules but not whether the percentages changed, so the SAG text decides
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Quality terms
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Wine With Seth: Superior → Reserva (+0.5° alcohol, oak optional) → Reserva Especial (+0.5°, oak required) → Reserva Privada (+1°, oak optional) → Gran Reserva (+1°, oak required); alcohol and oak rules, not minimum ageing periods
slides.2.content: Percentages and quality terms differ across sources, so check the SAG text before an exam.
slides.3.title: Costa, Entre Cordilleras, Andes
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Costa
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Coastal sites influenced by the Pacific
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Entre Cordilleras
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The central depression between the Andes and the Coastal Cordillera
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Andes
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The Andean piedmont; these three terms require at least 85% by volume from qualifying areas (Wine With Seth); sources date them to 1995 or 2011, so the year is not tested
slides.3.content: These three terms are west-to-east zones used alongside the north-to-south valleys.
slides.4.title: Diploma depth: the design logic of the DO system
slides.4.highlights.0.title: The 75% rule and big brands
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Origin, variety and vintage need only 75% compliance, letting large wineries blend across valleys and vintages to keep high-volume, low-priced brands consistent. The cost is looser label information: weaker consumer assurance than the 85% threshold common in the EU
slides.4.highlights.1.title: The blind spot of north–south valleys
slides.4.highlights.1.content: DOs follow valleys from north to south, but Chile’s biggest climatic contrast runs west to east: the coast is cooled by the Humboldt Current, the Andean side has altitude and wide diurnal swings, and the central depression is hottest. Within one valley, coastal and Andean wines can differ more than wines from neighbouring valleys
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Why Costa, Entre Cordilleras and Andes exist
slides.4.highlights.2.content: These three transversal terms are optional overlays on existing DOs (85% must come from the zone), filling in the east–west differences the north–south system misses; they can appear on the label together with the valley name
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Essay angle: law mirrors industry structure
slides.4.highlights.3.content: The loose 75% rule serves export-driven large groups; the transversal terms serve boutique producers seeking terroir expression. Their coexistence neatly shows Chile’s two tracks: volume and premium
slides.4.content: Reading a Chilean label: valley first (north–south), then Costa/Andes (east–west); together they describe the terroir.
Which body administers Chile's DO system?
The SAG, the agriculture and livestock service.
In which year was Decreto 464 published?
A. The central depression between the Andes and the Coastal Cordillera
Costa is the coast and Andes the piedmont.
What do Chile's Reserva-and-above quality terms mainly regulate?
A. Alcohol level and oak use
Alcohol and oak rules, not ageing time (Wine With Seth).
